facts.text: John Murphey began buying land north of River Road in the 1920s to create low‑density, privacy‑focused homes that preserved desert vegetation and mountain views.
In 1928 Murphey purchased a 7,000‑acre tract between North Oracle Road and Sabino Canyon in a federal land auction.
Swiss architect Josias Joesler was hired to bring Murphey’s vision to life, designing many of the early homes and the church that opened in 1936.
Saint Philip’s Church, founded in 1936 and donated land by Murphey, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Catalina Foothills area is defined as north of River Road, east of Oracle Road, and west of Sabino Creek, placing it within Tucson’s eastern foothills.
The Skyline Country Club opened in 1963, followed by La Paloma Resort and Ventana Canyon Resort in the 1980s, marking the area’s shift toward upscale recreation.
